intent: Grave-armour of a barrow king's guard: a closed-face helm winged and crested in tarnished bronze, a moss-eaten fur mantle over mould-black leather, and bold bronze at the breastplate, belt and pauldrons, so the winged head and green shoulders read first from the high camera.
requests: A mid-bronze colour between the dull plate and the scraped edge, for a large crown or pauldron plate that must catch the moon without reading as a worn strip.
A fur or fleece material (or a clumped fur builder) so a mantle does not read as a flat slab from the high camera.
A wedge or fan piece for a swept wing that reads from two angles in one part, instead of stepping a wing out of boxes.
